mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > 10% month-over-month AND UNRATE rises > 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
